transcript: Last night, I saw the Encores production of Urinetown at New York City Center. In the world of this musical, a longstanding drought has reached a point where private restrooms are no longer a thing. In typical fashion, a big corporation in conjunction with the government capitalizes off of this by charging a fee to use the public restrooms. As you might imagine, the citizens reach a breaking point and some stuff goes down. I thought this was cute with great performances, especially Jordan Fisher as Bobby Strong. Another highlight was Tiffany Mann who went on as Penelope last night. Now, I personally don't think the Urinetown score is good enough to be worthy of the Encores treatment, and I kind of think the City Center Main Stage is way too big of a house for a musical of this scale. But all that's really beside the point — this is a solid production and is as well directed as I think it can be. It leans into the satire without going overboard with it, and it has some really funny moments to the credit of the cast truly making the most of every line. I wouldn't consider this a must-see, but I would absolutely recommend it if you're a Jordan Fisher fan or a fan of the musical already. Urinetown is running through February 16th at New York City Center. With that, another program for my collection.
